title: Descent of coefficient-compatible functors
statement:
Let $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_E(S)$ be exact functors and let
$$
 \beta_{F/E}:T^S_{F/E}\Phi_E
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_FT^T_{F/E}
$$
be exact natural isomorphisms satisfying the unit, associator, and shift
equations of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Then they induce an exact
functor $\Phi:\mathcal P_T\to\mathcal P_S$. On a representative
$u:T^T_{M/E}K\to T^T_{M/F}L$, its value is represented by
$$
 T^S_{M/E}\Phi_EK\xrightarrow{\beta_{M/E}}
 \Phi_MT^T_{M/E}K\xrightarrow{\Phi_M(u)}
 \Phi_MT^T_{M/F}L\xrightarrow{\beta_{M/F}^{-1}}
 T^S_{M/F}\Phi_FL.
$$
This functor is, by [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], already a functor on the
$\Qlb$ coefficient categories $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ and
$\Dbc(S,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_S$. Compatible natural transformations and their
equations descend by the same formula.

In particular, the scalar-compatible families $(Rf_{*,E})_E$ and
$(Lg_E^*)_E$ descend to exact functors on $\Qlb$ coefficient categories, and
the finite-stage exchange maps descend to a natural transformation.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this descent of functors: the
ledger's verified entries contain no filtered-colimit-of-categories
statement — the nearest, the Chapter 61 coefficient entries 09BS, 09BT, 09C1
and 09C7, work with one fixed Noetherian coefficient ring — and the
blueprint adds the descent of scalar-compatible exact functors and of their
natural transformations to the $\Qlb$ coefficient categories, together with
the descended direct images, pullbacks and exchange maps. The closest
descent statements in Stacks, each fetched and quoted, are the universal
properties of a localization and of a Verdier quotient: Lemma 13.5.7 ([Tag
05R7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R7), an exact functor out of
$\mathcal D$ that inverts the multiplicative system factors uniquely and
exactly through $S^{-1}\mathcal D$) and Lemma 13.6.8 ([Tag
05RJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RJ), the same for the quotient
$\mathcal D/\mathcal B$ by a full triangulated subcategory), with Definition
13.6.1 ([Tag 05RB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RB), saturated,
i.e. thick, triangulated subcategory) and Definition 13.6.7 ([Tag
05RI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RI),
$\mathcal D/\mathcal B=S^{-1}\mathcal D$). Difference: a localization or
quotient inverts a multiplicative system inside one category and its
factorization needs no further data, whereas $\mathcal P_T$ is a filtered
colimit of categories and the functors descend with the explicit
$\beta$-isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] to $\mathcal A_E=\mathcal C_E(T)$, $\mathcal B_E=\mathcal C_E(S)$, $U=T^T$, $V=T^S$, $b=\beta$. Its unit and tower hypotheses are precisely the assumed ones. It gives the additive functor $(E,K)\mapsto(E,\Phi_EK)$ with the displayed representative formula, including independence of common stage and representative.

source.place: Proof, object and representative formulas and independence of common stage

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pair-functor-shift-coherence] to this functor, with the given exact stage shift comparisons: it supplies coherent shifts and shift-compatible $\kappa_E:\Phi j_E^T\simeq j_E^S\Phi_E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-distinguished-diagram-lifting], any distinguished triangle is isomorphic to $j_E^T\Delta$ for a distinguished stage triangle $\Delta$. Its image is isomorphic to $j_E^S\Phi_E\Delta$ via $\kappa_E$ on the vertices: the first two squares are naturality and the last is precisely shift compatibility. The latter triangle is distinguished since $\Phi_E$ and $j_E^S$ are exact, the inclusion by [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms]. Distinguishedness is invariant under triangle isomorphism, so $\Phi$ is exact. [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] identifies these pair categories with the stated coefficient categories.

source.place: Proof, exactness and identification with Qbar coefficient categories

proof.text: For compatible transformations use [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent], whose compatibility equation gives the components $[E,\eta_{E,K}]$ and their naturality. Identities and vertical composites have components $[E,1]$ and $[E,\theta_{E,K}\circ\eta_{E,K}]$. Its compatibility with composition of functor families identifies descended composites; applying the component formula to whiskerings gives horizontal composition. Equations hold componentwise already at $E$. The same argument applies to composites on different schemes.

source.place: Proof, compatible natural transformations and their equations

proof.text: [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] gives the exact rationalized direct images, completed pullbacks and exchange for the supplied constructibility-preserving integral operations. [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] gives their coherent comparisons and compatibility of the exchange with coefficient extension. Apply steps 1–3 to these families and their composites to obtain the claimed functors and exchange on the categories of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category].

source.place: Proof, final sentence: direct image, pullback and exchange

The item proof is now a 4-step assembly of 2170 characters, and the one new statement-only node, lem-weil-pbc-pair-functor-shift-coherence, carries the shift part of old step 4: integer-shift naturality, the zero/addition laws, and the shift compatibility of kappa_E that the third square of the image triangle needs. No argument is dropped. Old steps 1-3 and 5 (formulas, independence, additivity, transformations, composites, equations) are covered by the existing split node lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent. Its pair category, transport formula, unit/pentagon hypotheses, tower equation and compatibility equation match def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category and prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension exactly; I checked the types. That node is a declared tool use, it does not reach the item, and I accept it as a generic tool. Step 2 is correct: lem-weil-pbc-distinguished-diagram-lifting gives triangle ≅ j_M Delta through the identity vertex isomorphisms; kappa naturality gives the first two squares and the new node gives the third; Phi_M is exact, j_M is exact (thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms), and distinguished triangles are closed under isomorphism. Step 4 matches rational-transport (constructibility qualification kept) and scalar-extension (comparisons in the beta direction, exchange compatibility). The new node is true: naturality follows from the shift equation plus naturality of s_M, and kappa is the identity since beta_{E/E}=1 and T_{E/E}=id. Small cases (Phi=id; n=0; m=-n types) check out. No duplicate in the DAG; the near candidates are circular (they cite the item) or about other categories. No cycles, no SGA. Its statement matches the current main-20261015 statement and proof.md. proof.text:
Define $\Phi(E,K)=(E,\Phi_EK)$ on objects and, on a representative $(M,u)$,
by the displayed composite in $\mathcal C_M(S)$. The value is independent of
$M$: for $M\subset N$ the $\beta$-isomorphisms transport the composite for
$u$ to the composite for $u_N$, using the unit and associator equations of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] which the $\beta$'s satisfy; equivalent
representatives give equal composites at the witnessing stage by those
equations, so $\Phi$ is well defined on the morphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. It is additive, the composites
being exact functors and exact natural isomorphisms of exact natural
transformations, and exact (finite-stage exactness of the $\Phi_E$ and the
$T$'s makes the composite exact on distinguished triangles); natural
transformations and their equations descend by that formula by the
equivariance with the $\beta$'s. By [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] this is
already the descent to the $\Qlb$ coefficient categories
($\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ and $\Dbc(S,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_S$); no extension
to an envelope is needed. The families $(Rf_{*,E})_E$ and $(Lg_E^*)_E$ carry
the scalar-extension isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] as the
data $\beta$, so they descend to exact functors on the $\Qlb$ coefficient
categories, and the finite-stage exchange maps, being compatible with scalar
extension, descend to a natural transformation.
